clue.text: Primarily salvaged rubbish back page before editor freaked out

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so only the opening letter of the next word counts
going back means the word before it is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to rubbish something is to pan it, criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: Someone panics when a scrap of rescued rubbish turns up ahead of the editor's back page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubbish' looks like a noun beside salvaged, but here it is the verb meaning criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to lose one's composure suddenly, so someone who snapped has lost control or flipped.

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked, split herring

explanation.surface: A ship's master has a single smoked fish for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a British breakfast staple: a herring split and smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a ship or leader of a team, a captain.

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
fortissimo, the musical marking for very loud
a programme that is broadcast airs

explanation.surface: A grown-up loudly announces details of romances.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs are romantic or sexual liaisons, often illicit relationships.

clue.text: Alarm is cursed, initially, after upsetting sleep

indicators.note: upsetting means turning over, so in a down clue the word is flipped

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so first letters of the two words are taken

parts.note: first letters of is and cursed

explanation.surface: An alarm clock is cursed for disturbing someone's sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden fear, synonymous with alarm as a state of fright.

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: An instruction to put a spare tablet away.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish or go away, so it can stand for leave.

clue.text: Introduction of speed enthralling match official

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one word grips the other inside it

explanation.surface: A referee's dramatic early entrance reads like a sports report about pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A preface is the opening section of a book, an introductory statement before the main text.

clue.text: Part of bicycle perhaps somewhat scraped a leg

indicators.note: somewhat means a portion of, so the letters sit within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cyclist grazes a leg on a bike component.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal is the foot lever that drives a bicycle; perhaps signals that pianos and cars have them too.

clue.text: Little energy, cross and brooding, dear?

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy, and a single letter is little
a cross is shaped like the letter X

explanation.surface: Someone low on energy, grumpy and moody, is addressed as darling.
explanation.walkthrough: Dear reads as a term of endearment; it means costly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear in the sense of high-priced is a synonym for costly.

clue.text: Almost everyone leaving country for another one

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
leaving means departing, so those letters are taken out of the next word

parts.note: a nation whose name holds the shortened word for everyone

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole population emigrates from one nation to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Country looks like the definition, but it is the starting word; another one, meaning another country, is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Another one stands for another nation, and Austria is a nation in central Europe.

clue.text: Radical old Tories meet on a regular basis

indicators.note: regular means at even intervals, so alternate letters are kept

explanation.surface: Hardline veteran Conservatives get together regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator works on both words. Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme and radical both describe views far from the political mainstream.

clue.text: At home, lover's keeping time for children

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so one piece is held inside another

parts.note: a fan is a lover of something, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A partner who stays home makes time for the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Infants are very young children, babies and toddlers.

clue.text: Plonk is knocked back in warehouse

indicators.note: knocked back means turned backwards, so the little word runs right to left
in places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: a depot is a storage warehouse

explanation.surface: Cheap wine gets drunk in a warehouse, since plonk is knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonk and knocked back suggest cheap wine being drunk; plonk is really the verb to put down heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To deposit is to set something down, just as to plonk is to put it down heavily.

indicators.note: in speech means as heard when spoken, not as written

parts.note: a principle is a fundamental reason or basis

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the central reasoning of a speech was.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words sound identical but are spelt differently; the -AL spelling is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Principal as an adjective means chief or most important, a synonym for main.

clue.text: Still going backwards crossing river, showing courage

indicators.note: going backwards means the word is read from end to start
crossing means straddling, so one piece sits across the other

parts.note: still and even both mean nevertheless, as in 'even so'

explanation.surface: Someone bravely keeps reversing across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: Still here is the adverb 'even' (still better, even better), not motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means boldness or daring, a synonym for courage.

parts.note: someone who stirred got up, rose

explanation.surface: A bartender stirs some small drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Stirred looks like cocktail-making, but it means woke and got up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosés are pink wines, so the plural names glasses or bottles of that drink.

indicators.note: something hugged is held within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to type is to print text

explanation.surface: A handsome sort is embraced by a woman named Carol.
explanation.walkthrough: Carol looks like a name, and dashing like handsome; both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing in the sense of rushing is the same as sprinting, running at full speed.

clue.text: Get rid of dodgy email in the husband's shed

indicators.note: dodgy means unsound or suspect, so these letters are disordered
something shed is cast off, so that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Someone tells you to delete the suspicious email found in a husband's garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Shed looks like the garden building, but it is the verb meaning cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate is to remove completely, which is what getting rid of something means.

clue.text: Unaware Ed could be hidden here?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not knowing about something
second, cryptic meaning: a place where the letters of the name Ed lie concealed

explanation.surface: A man called Ed is oblivious, perhaps hiding somewhere unlit.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half points at the answer's own letters: E and D sit side by side across THE DARK, so Ed is literally hidden in the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the dark is an idiom for being uninformed or ignorant of something.

clue.text: Show the significance of topless dramatist with pert bust

indicators.note: topless means without its top, so the first letter is removed
bust means broken, so these letters are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky scene about a playwright with a perky bosom needs explaining.
explanation.walkthrough: Topless and bust create a racy picture; they are deletion and anagram signals.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret is to explain the meaning of something, to show what it signifies.

parts.note: hot and in both mean fashionable
a stead is a place, as in 'in his stead'

explanation.surface: Someone says they would prefer a warmer spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead and rather both mean as an alternative, in preference.

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A small child takes wobbly steps.
explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like a description of the toddler; it means curt.
explanation.definitionFit: To totter is to move unsteadily, as if about to fall.

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so that letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A nurse overlooks a patient's fever, and Edward's story is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Ended means finished or brought to a close, the same as concluded.

clue.text: Groom and bride abandoning bishop, exhausted

indicators.note: to groom is to tidy and rearrange, so these letters are put into a new order
abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: The bride and groom walk out on the bishop, worn out by the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Groom looks like the bridegroom, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Drained means emptied of energy, a synonym for exhausted.

indicators.note: wound as in twisted, so these letters are wrapped into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor examines an injury and dresses the daughter's wound.
explanation.walkthrough: Wound looks like an injury; read it as the past of wind, meaning twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: A wound that is dressed has been covered with a bandage or dressing.

parts.note: to pose for a portrait is to sit for it

explanation.surface: A model posed for a painter wearing shiny fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Satin is a smooth silky fabric with a glossy surface on one side.

parts.note: a Dane is a European from Denmark

explanation.surface: A big continental hound is described.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a breed of very tall dog.

indicators.note: a person wearing clothes is inside them, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Gap is a clothing retailer, with possessive S

explanation.surface: A boy tries on trousers from a high-street chain.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like trousers or underwear; it is the verb meaning breathes hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Gasps and pants both mean breathes quickly and heavily.

indicators.note: something eating takes food inside it, so one piece swallows the other

parts.note: to tout is to advertise or push

explanation.surface: A restaurant pushes its fish of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Trout is a freshwater fish of the salmon family.

indicators.note: fighting letters are in turmoil, thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A witness reports men brawling with their opponents.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies are opponents or foes, the same as adversaries.

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: as and while both mean during the time that
a mount is a horse for riding

explanation.surface: A rider does arithmetic while sitting astride a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To amount to is to total, so a sum that amounts to something adds up to it.

clue.text: Demeans oneself embracing Starmer's opening plans

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: to deign is to condescend, lowering oneself

indicators.note: an opening is a beginning, so only the first letter counts

parts.note: first letter of Starmer, the UK Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A political jibe that the Prime Minister lowers himself to embrace certain plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Designs are schemes or intentions, synonyms for plans.

parts.note: Katy Perry the pop singer; maybe flags her as one example of a Perry
to carry out a task is to do it

explanation.surface: A pear drink or a singer is said to have done something about a bug.
explanation.walkthrough: Perry is also a cider made from pears, a likely false start.
explanation.definitionFit: A katydid is a North American bush cricket, named after its call.
